History:
- Chief complaint: Severe lower abdominal pain, ongoing for a few days, worsening; pain described as constant and around 8/10.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began several days ago; progressively worse; present most of the time.
- Location and character: Lower abdomen, midline, below the umbilicus; constant.
- Associated symptoms: Light pink vaginal bleeding/discharge; nausea sensation without vomiting; last menstrual period about 2–3 weeks ago; regular intercourse; on Implanon for ~1 year with occasional irregular bleeding; constipation last week (resolved this week); drinks a lot; no fever, no dyspnea.
- Menstrual/contraception history: LMP ~2 weeks ago; Implanon in place; periods described as regular but with occasional irregular bleeding.
- Obstetric history: No pregnancies to date; prior pregnancy test about a month ago; pregnancy status not known today.
- Social/history: Sexually active; husband at home; occupation: school teacher; recent travel abroad (over a year ago).
- Plan stated by clinician: In-person abdominal examination to further evaluate; pregnancy test today; arrange appointment via support line; instructions to return if pain worsens or if fluids cannot be kept down.

Past Medical History:
- Allergies: Amoxicillin allergy.
- Medications: Implanon contraception.
- Chronic illnesses, prior hospitalizations, surgeries: Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Not recorded in the transcript.
- Not yet performed: abdominal examination, pelvic examination, vitals, or other exam findings.

Impression:
- Primary impression: Acute lower abdominal pain in a reproductive-age woman with light vaginal bleeding; requires evaluation to exclude pregnancy-related etiologies and pelvic pathology.
- Top plausible diagnoses (consistent with transcript):
  - Ovarian cyst rupture / corpus luteum cyst – lower midline, constant pain with concurrent light vaginal bleeding.
  - Pregnancy-related: ectopic pregnancy or threatened abortion (early intrauterine pregnancy) – vaginal bleeding with lower abdominal pain; pregnancy status to be confirmed today.
  - Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) – lower abdominal pain with vaginal discharge/bleeding in a sexually active young woman.
- Conflict noted: none.

Management Plan:
- Immediate actions done or advised:
  - Arrange in-person face-to-face abdominal examination in clinic; clinician to assess abdomen.
  - Perform a pregnancy test today; if positive, patient to be seen urgently.
  - Instruct patient to call support line to book the appointment.
  - Advise that if symptoms worsen significantly or if unable to keep fluids down, seek urgent care before the scheduled visit.
- DDx-informed steps are limited to those supported by transcript context (abdominal exam and pregnancy testing).

Patient Summary:
- A 2x-year-old (23-year-old per transcript) woman with several days of worsening lower abdominal pain and light vaginal bleeding while on Implanon, with LMP ~2 weeks ago. Plan includes in-person abdominal exam and a pregnancy test today; urgent evaluation if positive pregnancy test or symptoms escalate.

Key Takeaways:
- Schedule and complete an in-person abdominal exam promptly.
- Obtain a pregnancy test today; positive result requires urgent evaluation.
- Contact the support line to arrange the clinic visit; seek urgent care if pain worsens or if you cannot keep fluids down.

Next Steps:
- Complete the in-person abdominal examination as scheduled.
- Perform pregnancy testing today; communicate results promptly.
- Depending on exam and test results, pursue appropriate further evaluation (e.g., pelvic ultrasound) as indicated by findings.
